title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page finishes a sentence from the previous page (ms. p. 389). The setting is the 'équation des lacets' programme, i.e. the study of loop-preserving automorphisms of the profinite π_1 of U_{0,3} = P^1 − {0,1,∞}.

Grothendieck uses the isomorphism M'_{1,1,Q} ≃ U_{0,3,Q}. Here M'_{1,1} is the moduli of elliptic curves with a Jacobi (level-2, Legendre) rigidification, and λ is the coordinate.

The question is whether the outer Galois action of Γ_Q (or of Γ_{Q,T}) on π̂_{0,3} lifts to a genuine action on the larger group Ŝ^+_{0,3} ≃ SL(2,Z)^. That group also carries the ±1 coming from the elliptic involution. The 'general yoga' says such lifts should correspond to rational points of the stack over the S_3-symmetric point λ = 1/2 of U_{0,3}(Q). Concretely, they correspond to elliptic curves over Q with a level-2 Jacobi rigidification and λ = 1/2.

The ambiguity in choosing such a curve is the set of quadratic twists, H^1(Q, ±1) = Hom(Γ_Q, ±1). This matches the ambiguity in the lift. Grothendieck concludes that the yoga is correct and that there is no truly privileged lift, even over Γ_{Q,T}.

Lifts exist because such curves exist. On this page he picks the simplest one, equation (22): y^2 = x(x−1)(x−1/2), the Legendre curve at λ = 1/2 ('et voilà le choix fait !').

He then leaves a programme open: make this lift explicit 'dans un formulaire calculatoire', i.e. give explicit formulas for the Galois action on SL(2,Z)^ determined by this base curve, 'si ce n'est pas sans espoir', to be examined later. The next page starts a new section, a recapitulation of notation for loop automorphisms of π̂_{0,3} and Ŝ^+_{0,3} (the groups M̃_{0,3}, Ñ_{0,3}, the map to S_3).
errors: No mathematical error. Check: with x = u + 1/2 the curve becomes y^2 = u^3 − u/4, a quadratic twist of y^2 = x^3 − x (by 2). So j = 1728 (CM by Z[i]), consistent with λ = 1/2 being the point of U_{0,3} with a nontrivial S_3-stabilizer (fixed by λ ↦ 1 − λ). 'Simplest' is a matter of taste: any quadratic twist (e.g. y^2 = x^3 − x itself, after renormalizing the Legendre coordinate) works equally well, as he himself notes.

ideas.what: Lifts of the Galois outer action from π̂_{0,3} to SL(2,Z)^ (including the ±1 of the elliptic involution) are classified by rational points over λ = 1/2 of the level-2 elliptic moduli stack. The ambiguity is the torsor of quadratic twists, H^1(Q, ±1).
ideas.modern_name: Sections/splittings of the arithmetic fundamental group sequence of M_{1,1}[2] given by rational points; quadratic-twist torsor of the μ_2-gerbe M_{1,1} → coarse space
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore of anabelian geometry; Galois actions on SL(2,Z)^ studied by Nakamura, Ihara, Lochak–Schneps, Hain–Matsumoto (1990s–2000s)
ideas.where_published: Not in the Esquisse in this form as far as I know; the general section/rational-point yoga is in the 1983 letter to Faltings

ideas.what: Concrete choice of base curve y^2 = x(x−1)(x−1/2) (Legendre λ = 1/2, j = 1728) to fix the lift.
ideas.modern_name: Rational base point on M_{1,1}[2] / CM curve as base point

ideas.what: Programme to write an explicit formula for the resulting Galois action on SL(2,Z)^ (or Ŝ^+_{0,3}).
ideas.modern_name: Explicit Galois/GT action on profinite SL(2,Z) / B_3 and on π_1 of once-punctured elliptic curves
ideas.usually_credited_to: Nakamura (explicit formulas for Galois action on π_1 of M_{1,1} and of punctured elliptic curves, 1990s); Lochak–Schneps; Hain–Matsumoto

missed.claim: Grothendieck wanted an explicit 'formulaire calculatoire' for the Galois lift on SL(2,Z)^ normalized by the λ = 1/2 Legendre curve. He left it as a task for later.
missed.quote: Il resterait à essayer de l'expliciter dans un formulaire calculatoire, si ce n'est pas sans espoir.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This was essentially carried out later and independently (Nakamura's explicit formulas; GT actions on B_3/SL_2). The specific normalization through a j = 1728 base curve and its twist ambiguity is a minor historical point rather than a new result.

deep.surprise_reason: A clean, correct observation tying lifts of the Galois action to quadratic twists of a level-2 elliptic curve at λ = 1/2. It is natural, essentially folklore, and its explicit version was developed later by others; it is only of historical interest.
transcription_corrections: Equation (22): the exponent of y is overwritten but reads y^2; the equation is y^2 − x(x−1)(x−1/2) = 0.
Line 4 of the text reads '& voilà le choix fait !' (with a leading dash).
'[-par-]' crossed out before 'dans un formulaire calculatoire' is correct; 'si ce n'est[?] pas sans espoir' is plausible.
